>>> Water molecules are polar, meaning they have a partial positive charge on the hydrogen atoms and a partial negative charge on the oxygen atoms.  
>>> When water freezes, these molecules form a hexagonal crystalline structure held together by hydrogen bonds.  
>>> In liquid water, molecules move more freely and are closer together, but in ice, the hydrogen bonds create a rigid, open lattice that increases the volume of the substance.  
>>> This open structure makes ice less dense than liquid water, which is why it floats.  
>>> This property is unusual because most substances become denser when they transition from liquid to solid, but water’s hydrogen bonding causes the opposite effect.
